<p class="pg-lede">Source-specific nuclear power and small modular reactor techno-economic parameters and inputs, preserving printed values, technical and monetary bases, source terms and paper cross-references. Includes reference-plant estimates, fleet observations, design descriptions, policy parameters and regulatory charges.</p>
<p class="ref-meta"><span class="chip">Version 0.1</span> <span class="chip">Checked 2026-11-13</span> <span class="chip">77 quantities</span></p>
<p class="ref-actions"><a href="nuclear-v0.1.csv" class="btn-solid">Download versioned CSV</a> <a href="index.html#cite" class="btn-outline">How to cite</a></p>
<p>United States focus; Canadian-filed vendor material is labeled as supplementary design context. Coverage: 1986/... January 1986 decommissioning-assurance cost bases, 2020–2025 fleet observations, 2026 policy and regulatory records, 2030-onward reference scenarios and construction-start phaseout cases through 2036 onward.</p>
<p>Values retain their source-specific bases; costs have not been escalated or converted. NR means not reported or not established, never zero. FOAK means first-of-a-kind; BOAK means between first- and nth-of-a-kind; NOAK means nth-of-a-kind. Blank numeric fields are missing values. Suffixes separate scenarios or years while retaining the common N-number. Verification of a printed value does not establish realized cost, performance or eligibility.</p>
<p>The paper column labels input use, citation provenance, numerical correspondence and contextual discussion separately. Input use identifies a stated model assumption; it does not establish the original source. Context is not a numerical input. Only examined public versions are linked, with version-specific locators. All expanded basis and locator text is present in the page and downloads.</p>

<section class="fx-sec" aria-labelledby="read-before-using">
<div class="fx-head"><h2 id="read-before-using">Read before using</h2></div>
<dl class="ref-risks">
<dt>Overnight versus total capital</dt><dd>Record IDC/AFUDC, escalation during construction, owner’s costs, contingency, initial fuel and interconnection separately. A table labelled “Total Capital Cost” may still be an overnight total.</dd>
<dt>FOAK versus BOAK versus NOAK</dt><dd>Preserve the source’s term. Distinguish first design, first country deployment, first site unit and repeat factory production.</dd>
<dt>$/kWe versus $/kWth</dt><dd>Never substitute one for the other without an explicit efficiency and boundary.</dd>
<dt>Net versus gross output</dt><dd>Record auxiliary demand and whether the denominator is generator output, plant export or delivered customer power.</dd>
<dt>Capacity factor versus availability</dt><dd>Fleet CF includes generation behavior; availability describes whether equipment can operate. Neither alone establishes data-center service reliability.</dd>
<dt>Ramp rate versus operating envelope</dt><dd>Identify rated-power denominator, electric versus thermal power, permitted range, time resolution and fuel-cycle conditions.</dd>
<dt>Design life versus licence term</dt><dd>Keep technical life, amortization life, analysis horizon and regulatory permission in separate fields.</dd>
<dt>Fuel price versus fuel cost</dt><dd>Uranium and SWU purchase prices do not determine $/MWh without enrichment, tails, fabrication, burnup, efficiency and inventory assumptions.</dd>
<dt>Production versus investment credit</dt><dd>§45Y applies to qualifying production; §48E applies to qualified investment. Percentage bonuses and percentage-point adders differ.</dd>
<dt>Reactor temperature versus usable heat</dt><dd>Include steam pressure, phase, extraction location, return conditions and temperature losses.</dd>
<dt>Footprint versus site</dt><dd>Separate building envelope, protected area, owner-controlled area, construction laydown, cooling systems and EPZ.</dd>
<dt>Vendor claim versus reviewed value</dt><dd>Government hosting does not make vendor content a government endorsement. Design approval does not establish commercial performance.</dd>
<dt>Decommissioning assurance versus expenditure</dt><dd>A regulatory minimum funding formula is not a complete project cost estimate.</dd>
<dt>Historical order versus current entitlement</dt><dd>A dated FERC order cannot establish today’s contractual limit without checking subsequent proceedings.</dd>
<dt>Verification and source conflicts</dt><dd>Transcription verification confirms what a document prints. The separate underlying-evidence and conflict fields describe the limits of that evidence. Neither a model input nor a vendor design claim is independently demonstrated operating performance.</dd>
<dt>Policy scope and payment</dt><dd>Qualifying capacity additions at older facilities can fall within §45Y/§48E. Domestic-content requirements can affect elective payment as well as bonus eligibility; statutory exceptions and waivers must be checked.</dd>
<dt>Source versions</dt><dd>Edition, revision, release date, retrieval date and document SHA-256 are separate fields. A checksum identifies retrieved bytes, not accuracy; live HTML navigation can change without changing a cited table.</dd>
</dl>
</section>
<section class="fx-sec" aria-labelledby="disagreements">
<div class="fx-head"><h2 id="disagreements">Where sources disagree</h2></div>
<div class="ref-table-scroll" role="region" aria-label="Source disagreements" tabindex="0"><table class="ref-comparison" data-quarto-disable-processing="true"><caption>Source-version and definition differences</caption><thead><tr><th scope="col">Issue</th><th scope="col">Published values and sources</th><th scope="col">Interpretation</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><th scope="row">Large-reactor overnight capital</th><td>7,861 $/kW net (N01); 5,750 $/kWe (N07).<br><a href="#source-S1">S1</a> · <a href="#source-S2">S2</a></td><td>Different 2023/2022 dollar bases, plant scales, cost accounts and maturity definitions. Retain the source-specific estimates without averaging.</td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row">SMR overnight capital</th><td>8,936 $/kW net (N03); 8,000 $/kWe in Table A-1 (N08).<br><a href="#source-S1">S1</a> · <a href="#source-S2">S2</a></td><td>EIA specifies a six-module NOAK plant; INL describes a generalized 300-MWe BOAK category. These are different plant and maturity assumptions.</td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row">INL Moderate SMR capital conflict</th><td>Table A-1: 8,000 $/kWe; Table 31: 7,750 $/kWe.<br><a href="#source-S2">S2</a> · <a href="#source-S35">S35</a></td><td>Unresolved internal conflict. N08 preserves the Rev. 0 Table A-1 value with a conflict flag; no canonical replacement is established. The July 2024 document also prints both values; its cover says Revision 2 and its internal title page says Revision 1.</td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row">Liftoff report editions</th><td>March 2023: FOAK 9,000 and NOAK 3,600 $/kW; September 2024: early-of-a-kind 7,000–20,000 $/kW.<br><a href="#source-S4">S4</a> · <a href="#source-S5">S5</a></td><td>Different scenario constructions and editions; the later range is not a revision of the earlier NOAK input.</td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row">ATB and INL inputs</th><td>INL candidate ATB recommendations; ATB 2024 narrative assumptions.<br><a href="#source-S2">S2</a> · <a href="#source-S3">S3</a></td><td>A recommendation in an INL report does not show that an ATB workbook release adopted it unchanged.</td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row">Construction clocks</th><td>EIA: 52/42 months (large LWR/SMR); ATB Moderate: 82/55 months.<br><a href="#source-S1">S1</a> · <a href="#source-S3">S3</a></td><td>Reference plants and scenarios differ. EIA reports development time separately: construction time is not total project lead time.</td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row">INL Moderate large-reactor fuel cost</th><td>Table A-1: 10.3 $/MWh; fuel discussion: 10.2 $/MWh.<br><a href="#source-S2">S2</a></td><td>Unresolved internal difference. N18 contains the Advanced and Conservative scenarios; no Moderate midpoint is supplied.</td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row">INL future-cost endpoints</th><td>Advanced-scenario large-reactor/SMR assignments in Table A-1 and Table 54 differ.<br><a href="#source-S2">S2</a></td><td>Disputed future-cost endpoints are outside this edition; reconciliation requires a revised document or erratum.</td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row">Heat delivery boundaries</th><td>Representative reactor outlets, coolant core exits and reference-model steam headers.<br><a href="#source-S3">S3</a> · <a href="#source-S14">S14</a> · <a href="#source-S15">S15</a></td><td>Different fluids and locations; reactor outlet temperature does not establish delivered process-steam temperature.</td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row">Xe-100 reference-model steam header</th><td>Table 9: 565.5°C and 161.4 bar; prose: 565°C and 160 bar.<br><a href="#source-S15">S15</a></td><td>Table/prose discrepancy; explanation not given. N44 retains Table 9 and marks the conflict. Pressure reference (gauge/absolute) remains NR.</td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row">BWRX-300 output convention</th><td>Workshop sheet: 300 MWe net; Rev. F includes both gross and net descriptions.<br><a href="#source-S29">S29</a> · <a href="#source-S33">S33</a></td><td>Keep the exact document label and version. No parasitic-load adjustment is inferred from the product name.</td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row">Tax-credit vintages</th><td>2026 indexed amounts and statutory nominal amounts have different roles.<br><a href="#source-S17">S17</a> · <a href="#source-S18">S18</a> · <a href="#source-S19">S19</a> · <a href="#source-S20">S20</a> · <a href="#source-S21">S21</a></td><td>Annual indexing and statutory amendments remain dated. Apply the amount and eligibility conditions for the relevant year together.</td></tr>
</tbody></table></div>
</section>
<section class="fx-sec" aria-labelledby="gaps">
<div class="fx-head"><h2 id="gaps">Gaps</h2></div>
<p>Public-source coverage still needed for comparable inputs:</p><dl class="ref-risks">
<dt>ATB nuclear cost workbook</dt><dd>The narrative chapter is included; a cell-level cost export is still needed before adding ATB capital-cost records. <a href="https://atb.nlr.gov/electricity/2024/nuclear">Public reference</a></dd>
<dt>INL revision reconciliation</dt><dd>Internal capital, fuel and future-cost differences require comparison with subsequent revisions or errata. <a href="https://gain.inl.gov/content/uploads/4/2024/11/INL-RPT-24-77048-Meta-Analysis-of-Adv-Nuclear-Reactor-Cost-Estimations.pdf">Public reference</a></dd>
<dt>Plant-specific flexibility</dt><dd>Public design- and fuel-cycle-specific operating constraints are needed for load following and ramp rates. Historical summaries do not establish licensed plant limits. <a href="https://europeanutilityrequirements.eu/fr/eur-document-full-text">Public reference</a></dd>
<dt>Licensing milestones</dt><dd>Licensing pathway and milestone definitions require separate evidence; executive deadlines do not establish observed approval duration. <a href="https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2025-05-29/html/2025-09798.htm">Public reference</a></dd>
<dt>All-in U.S. SMR capital cost</dt><dd>A consistently scoped commercial benchmark remains unavailable here. Financing, owner costs and shared-site allocation need explicit treatment. <a href="https://www.eia.gov/analysis/studies/powerplants/capitalcost/pdf/capital_cost_AEO2025.pdf">Public reference</a></dd>
<dt>Advanced-reactor operating costs</dt><dd>Technology-specific staffing, fuel cycles and maintenance need stronger public evidence; generic SMR estimates are not interchangeable across HTGR, SFR and MSR designs. <a href="https://gain.inl.gov/content/uploads/4/2024/11/INL-RPT-24-77048-Meta-Analysis-of-Adv-Nuclear-Reactor-Cost-Estimations.pdf">Public reference</a></dd>
<dt>Delivered process heat</dt><dd>Pressure reference, return temperature, enthalpy states, delivery distance and extraction penalties remain necessary for a project heat balance. <a href="https://inldigitallibrary.inl.gov/content/uploads/50/2026/04/Sort_106989.pdf">Public reference</a></dd>
<dt>Current complete-site footprints</dt><dd>Historical protected-area claims do not establish current application-specific total land, cooling or construction needs. <a href="https://api.cnsc-ccsn.gc.ca/dms/digital-medias/CMD-24-H3-Ref-R1-9-GEH-005N9751-BWRX-300-General-Description-Rev-F.pdf/object">Public reference</a></dd>
<dt>Decommissioning estimates</dt><dd>Site-specific expenditure estimates and advanced-reactor end-state assumptions are needed in addition to statutory financial assurance. <a href="https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/CFR-2025-title10-vol1/pdf/CFR-2025-title10-vol1-sec50-75.pdf">Public reference</a></dd>
<dt>Current co-location arrangements</dt><dd>Later FERC orders, tariffs and agreements must be checked for a contemporary project; the November 2024 order is historical. <a href="https://www.ferc.gov/sites/default/files/2024-11/20241101-3061_ER24-2172-000.pdf">Public reference</a></dd>
</dl>
</section>

<section class="fx-sec" aria-labelledby="downloads">
<div class="fx-head"><h2 id="downloads">Downloads</h2></div>
<ul><li><a href="nuclear-v0.1.csv">CSV — version 0.1</a></li><li><a href="nuclear-latest.csv">CSV — latest edition</a></li><li><a href="nuclear-sources.json">Source register and handbook metadata (JSON)</a></li></ul>
<p>The CSV has one quantity per record, with its applicable technology, scenario and year stated. Printed and numerical values are separate; blank numerical fields are missing, NR is not reported, and false explicitly means excluded. The paper_use column is a JSON array of paper keys, match types and version-specific locators. Source IDs separated by semicolons resolve to the register. No implied unit conversion is applied.</p>
<p>The nuclear CSV separately records transcription verification, underlying evidence, source conflicts and numerical-field interpretation. Source editions, revisions, release dates, publishers, retrieval dates and document SHA-256 values travel with each row. Semicolon-separated source IDs resolve to the accompanying JSON register; expanded bibliographic fields retain each source’s full text. NR denotes an unreported date or revision; it is not a date inferred from access. Document checksums identify source bytes, not independently validated engineering performance.</p>
<p>Li, H. (2026). Nuclear and SMR techno-economic parameters and inputs: Reference data handbook. Version 0.1. https://henryutd2021.github.io/reference-data/nuclear.html. Accessed [date], records [IDs].</p>
</section>
<section class="fx-sec" aria-labelledby="updates">
<div class="fx-head"><h2 id="updates">Update cadence</h2></div>
<p>This schedule describes planned source review; last checked 2026-11-13. Historical editions retain their original bases.</p><dl class="ref-risks">
<dt>EIA fleet capacity factors</dt><dd>Check monthly; append annual values when available and retain release vintage and preliminary/final status.</dd>
<dt>Uranium and enrichment prices</dt><dd>Annual release and revisions; retain the reissue date.</dd>
<dt>EIA capital costs, AEO and ATB</dt><dd>Each release; retain historical editions and their cost bases.</dd>
<dt>INL and DOE reports</dt><dd>Each revision, erratum or replacement; reconcile conflicts explicitly.</dd>
<dt>Tax-credit amounts and eligibility</dt><dd>Annual IRS indexing and immediate review after legislation or substantive Treasury/IRS guidance.</dd>
<dt>NRC licensing status and review schedules</dt><dd>Quarterly and at rulemaking or licensing milestones; distinguish publication and effective dates.</dd>
<dt>NRC hourly fees</dt><dd>Each annual final fee rule, including the actual implementation date.</dd>
<dt>Vendor design records</dt><dd>Each filing or design revision; retain superseded versions.</dd>
<dt>FERC arrangements</dt><dd>Each relevant order, tariff amendment or agreement.</dd>
<dt>Paper cross-references</dt><dd>Corrections or a new public version; preserve the examined version and its locators.</dd>
</dl>
</section>
